1	# GV-1 managed policy + GV-5 admin controls: implementation plan (read-only planning pass, 2026-11-22, code read at release/v1.3.0 ~65dc4fe4; verify every file:line by reading)
2	
3	## Facts about today's code
4	- `.nexus-security.json`: SecurityManager.loadPolicy, cli/src/security.ts ~:354-388 (existsSync + readFileSync + JSON.parse, follows symlinks, no size bound). FAILS OPEN: a bare `catch {}` (~:376-378) falls to the defaults with no message, silently dropping the project's own tightenings. Keys (SecurityPolicy ~:135-143): blockedCommands, protectedPaths, allowedDomains, verificationPaths.{mode, extra, allow}; modes off|record|approve|block (default approve). "Untrusted can only tighten": parseVerificationPolicy(raw, trusted) ~:238-254.
5	- Workspace trust: a list of real paths in ~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json (cli/src/workspace_trust.ts); NO content hash anywhere; NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1 grants trust.
6	- CS-9 command rules: cli/src/core/command_rules.ts (allow:0, prompt:1, forbidden:2; strictest wins; strict parsing) but LOADING fails open (agent.ts ~:1546-1555). `prompt` is skipped under full access (dispatch_tool_call.ts ~:448).
7	- Approval mode precedence: buildConfig, cli/src/config.ts ~:440-468 (read-only > --yes (auto + fullAccess) > --approve > --mode > NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE > review). There is NO --full-access flag. Runtime changes go through NexusAgent.setApprovalMode (agent.ts ~:745-760). ApprovalPolicy.requiresDecision: cli/src/core/approval_policy.ts ~:29-88 (full access returns false first).
8	- MCP choke point exists: McpClientManager connections (cli/src/mcp.ts ~:606, :621, :654); the server is spawned at connect(), so a gate must sit before construction. Plugins: loadPluginFile, cli/src/plugins.ts ~:96-117; a plugin's NAME is known only after its code ran, so an allowlist must key on the file (path or SHA-256) before import().
9	- No TOML parser in the repo, its dependencies (commander, dotenv, ora, picocolors) or Node's standard library.
10	- Hardened-reader precedent to copy: readOperatorConfigDocument, cli/src/config.ts ~:633-681 (lstat, no symlink, O_NOFOLLOW, fstat re-check, 64 KiB bound, version check, unknown key rejected). Root-owner check precedent: cli/src/sandbox.ts ~:469. Non-blocking open: cli/src/core/checkout_trust.ts ~:32-39. writePrivateFile: cli/src/core/durable_file.ts ~:120.
11	
12	## Format decision: a strict hand-written TOML SUBSET at D16's paths (/etc/nexus/policy.toml, ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml)
13	Why not JSON: JSON.parse silently takes the last duplicate key (`{"strict":true,"strict":false}` is false), so JSON would need a custom scanner too; TOML allows comments; D16 names .toml.
14	Grammar ACCEPTED: UTF-8, LF or CRLF, no BOM, no control characters except tab; blank lines; `#` comments (full-line or trailing); root `key = value` lines before any table; `[table]` headers, single level; keys and table names match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*; values: a basic string "..." on one line with only the \" and \\ escapes; true / false; a non-negative decimal integer; an array of basic strings (may span lines, trailing comma and comments allowed).
15	REJECTED, each with `line N`: literal or multi-line strings, any other escape; floats, signs, hex, underscores, dates; inline tables, dotted or quoted keys, [[...]], nested or mixed arrays; duplicate key, duplicate table; anything after a value except a comment; strings over 1024 characters, arrays over 500 items, files over 64 KiB.
16	Output {root, tables} with a line number per key; the parser is schema-agnostic; the VALIDATOR rejects unknown tables and keys. About 180-220 lines. Tests: ~25 accepted documents; ~60 rejected documents asserting line and message; render-then-parse round trip for generated documents; a mutation loop asserting only PolicyParseError is ever thrown.
17	
18	## Schema: ONE normalized PolicyDocument for all tiers. Restrict-only is encoded in BOTH the types (no field can express a grant) and the merge (a lattice meet, proven by a generated table)
19	| Key | Type | Merge | Enforces |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| schema_version | int, required in managed tiers | n/a | a reader accepts only its supported set and fails closed on a higher one |
22	| approval.strict | bool | OR | shorthand for the next three |
23	| approval.disable_auto | bool | OR | mode auto from any source |
24	| approval.disable_yes | bool | OR | -y/--yes (including verify --yes) |
25	| approval.disable_full_access | bool | OR | any fullAccess source |
26	| approval.require_human | array of exec, write_workspace, egress | union | always ask, even under full access |
27	| verification.mode | approve or block ONLY | max | a floor; off and record are type errors |
28	| verification.protected | globs | union | extra protected paths |
29	| commands.forbid, commands.prompt | prefix strings such as "git push" | union | CS-9 rules; no allow key exists |
30	| commands.disable_allow_rules | bool | OR | drops the user's allow rules |
31	| paths.protected | patterns | union | |
32	| egress.inspector | record or block | max | floor over NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY |
33	| egress.allowed_domains | allowlist | intersection | |
34	| egress.secret_destinations | allowlist | intersection | |
35	| sandbox.required | bool | OR | |
36	| sandbox.forbid_network | bool | OR | |
37	| mcp.allow | allowlist: name, command:/abs/path, url:https://origin | intersection | |
38	| mcp.disable_workspace | bool | OR | |
39	| plugins.allow | allowlist: sha256:<hex>, file:/abs/path | intersection | |
40	| plugins.disable_workspace | bool | OR | |
41	| workspace.disable_env_trust | bool | OR | ignores NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE |
42	Allowlists: absent = unrestricted; present (even empty) = only the listed items; absent is the identity for intersection.
43	The project tier stays `.nexus-security.json`, mapped by an adapter into (a) a restrictive PolicyDocument part and (b) a separate ProjectRelaxations type (legacy mode off/record, verificationPaths.allow). Relaxations apply only when the workspace is trusted, integrity is MATCH, and no managed tier sets verification.mode.
44	
45	## Merge and attribution
46	mergePolicies(system?, user?, project?) -> EffectivePolicy, frozen. Because the merge is a meet, precedence cannot change the value; it decides ATTRIBUTION only: for a scalar, the deciding tier is the highest tier whose own value equals the effective value; each list element carries the first tier that contributed it; otherwise `default`. PolicySource = {tier: "system"|"user"|"project"|"operator-rules"|"default", file?, key, line?}. One renderer describeSource -> e.g. `[policy: system /etc/nexus/policy.toml approval.strict]`; every prompt and denial appends it, including `[policy: default]` ("the effective tier is printed beside every decision").
47	
48	## Modules (slice 1 = these three + tests + docs; NO existing file edited)
49	- cli/src/core/managed_policy.ts: pure types, validation, merge, clamp helpers, describeSource.
50	- cli/src/core/managed_policy_toml.ts: the parser.
51	- cli/src/core/managed_policy_load.ts: file-system reads with EVERY input explicit: loadManagedPolicy({systemPath, systemOwnerUid, userPath, userUid, workspace, trust, fs}). The production constant `/etc/nexus/policy.toml` lives in exactly one place, is not configurable by env, argv or setter, and that source file references neither process.env nor process.argv (a guard test asserts this).
52	
53	## Fail-closed rules: both managed tiers throw ManagedPolicyError {tier, file, code, line?}
54	| Condition | System tier | User tier |
55	|---|---|---|
56	| File absent | tier absent | tier absent |
57	| /etc/nexus exists but is not root-owned, or group/world-writable, or a symlink | refuse | n/a |
58	| Symlink (lstat or ELOOP) | refuse | refuse |
59	| Not a regular file (open with O_NONBLOCK) | refuse | refuse |
60	| EACCES, EIO, any other error | refuse | refuse |
61	| Over 64 KiB | refuse | refuse |
62	| Owner | must be uid 0 | must be euid or 0 |
63	| Mode has 0o022 bits | refuse | refuse |
64	| fstat dev/ino differs from lstat | refuse | refuse |
65	| Invalid UTF-8, BOM, NUL | refuse | refuse |
66	| Syntax error, duplicate, unknown table or key, wrong type, bad enum | refuse | refuse |
67	| Empty file or missing schema_version | refuse | refuse |
68	| schema_version above supported | refuse | refuse |
69	Exit code 2 (matches existing configuration failures). Stderr, two lines:
70	  nexus: managed policy error (system tier): /etc/nexus/policy.toml: line 7: unknown key 'approval.disable_yess'.
71	  Nexus will not start without this policy. Fix the file (root-owned; ask your administrator) and run `nexus doctor`. No setting or environment variable bypasses it.
72	The user-tier variant ends: `Fix it, or move it aside: mv ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml.bad`.
73	Recovery: --version, --help, `nexus doctor` and `nexus policy check` always run. The system tier has NO override of any kind. `doctor --fix` never touches policy files.
74	
75	## Project integrity (principle 5)
76	Store ~/.config/nexus/policy_trust.json (writePrivateFile), keyed by workspace real path, value {sha256, approvedAt}. Order: bounded no-follow read -> SHA-256 -> status -> strict parse -> split into the restrictive part and relaxations. Statuses: ABSENT, NEW, MATCH, MISMATCH, REMOVED (+ ENV_TRUSTED for NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1 unless workspace.disable_env_trust). The restrictive part ALWAYS applies (as today for untrusted workspaces). Relaxations apply only on trusted and MATCH. Interactive NEW or MISMATCH with relaxations: ask, show them, record on yes. Headless: never ask; drop the relaxations, apply the restrictive part, emit a notice, record it. A project parse error stays non-fatal but becomes LOUD: built-in defaults, no relaxations, a notice, a doctor warning.
77	
78	## GV-5 refusals (exit 2 at launch; runtime attempts are clamped with a notice naming the source)
79	--yes under disable_yes/strict; --mode auto or NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto under disable_auto; /mode auto, the "always" answer and sidecar always-approve (mode unchanged, the one call approved, notice); --sandbox none or no sandbox under sandbox.required (forced to auto + requireSandbox; explicit none refused); --sandbox-network or NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK under forbid_network; an MCP server not in mcp.allow is not started; a plugin not in plugins.allow is not imported. A managed `prompt` command rule holds under full access.
80	
81	## G-3 rules
82	No grant is expressible; the merge is a meet; relaxations are void where a managed tier speaks. An absent tier is the identity (deleting the user or project file never goes below the system tier). Only two fixed absolute paths are read as managed; nothing under the workspace or cwd. No environment variable names a policy path; NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE, NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE, NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK, NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY are clamped AFTER the merge. lstat + O_NOFOLLOW + fstat dev/ino comparison, loaded once, frozen. Every key addition bumps schema_version (rollout order: Nexus first, then policy). Residual risks to document: an unsandboxed shell running as the user can edit the user tier and policy_trust.json for the next run (only the system tier is tamper-resistant); an admitted in-process plugin can defeat any in-process control; a bare-name mcp.allow entry is spoofable (pin with command: or url:).
83	
84	## Tests (slice 1)
85	- managed_policy_toml.test.ts as above.
86	- managed_policy_merge.test.ts: GENERATED precedence table: per key, the Cartesian product of small domains across the three tiers (booleans 27 cases; list domains {absent, [], [a], [b], [a,b]} = 125 cases; verification mode also varies the project's legacy modes and trust state). Expected value and deciding tier come from an INDEPENDENT oracle per key type, not from the merge. Also idempotence, commutativity, associativity, monotonicity. "Project cannot loosen system": for every key and system value and every project document (trusted, env-trusted, legacy relaxations, malformed, absent) the effective value is at least as restrictive as the system value.
87	- managed_policy_load.test.ts: every row of the fail-closed table through the injected loader (fake fs / injected uids), asserting code and exact message. Guard test: the literal `/etc/nexus` appears in exactly one source file, which references neither process.env nor process.argv.
88	- managed_policy_integrity.test.ts: MATCH, MISMATCH, NEW, REMOVED, env trust with and without disable_env_trust; headless drops relaxations.
89	- Published schema (slice 1 or 4): docs/protocol/policy-v1.schema.json + POLICY_VERSIONS.json generated from PolicyDocument with cli/scripts/result_schema.mjs; a parity test.
90	- docs/MANAGED_POLICY.md: schema, grammar, precedence, fail-closed table, recovery path, residual risks.
91	
92	## Slices
93	1. Pure library, NO existing source file edited (above).
94	2. GV-1 enforcement: config.ts, security.ts, approval_policy.ts, dispatch_tool_call.ts, command_rules.ts, workspace_trust.ts, spine_handlers.ts, completion_oracle.ts + a real-CLI test helper (interpose fs for exactly /etc/nexus and /etc/nexus/policy.toml in a child started with `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e`, as cli/test/operator_config_startup.test.ts ~:33-49 does; production keeps NO test seam).
95	3. GV-5: mcp.ts, plugins.ts, repl.ts, sidecar.ts, slash/session_commands.ts + strict-mode tests.
96	4. Visibility: doctor.ts findings policy.system|user|project|effective, new policy_cli.ts (show|check|approve), published schema.
97	5. Files claimed by others as they free up: index.ts, agent.ts, types.ts, sandbox.ts, core/verify.ts, protocol.ts + protocol.rs, session_export.ts, run_contract.ts, manual, changelog, the G-3 policy suite.
98	
99	## Decisions taken (defaults accepted 2026-11-22)
100	TOML subset at D16's paths. System path is a constant, not configurable at build or run time. User tier fails closed too, with the move-aside recovery. Headless MISMATCH continues tighter (relaxations dropped), does not exit. Restrictions from an untrusted project file keep applying; relaxations never before trust and MATCH. CS-9 command_rules.json stays separate; managed tiers add forbid and prompt only. Exit code 2. Explicit flags that policy disables are refused at launch; runtime attempts are clamped with a notice. No migration needed for .nexus-security.json. Windows has no system tier (doctor says so).
101	
102	## Claimed by other agents when planned (re-check before each slice; import only)
103	cli/src/agent.ts, index.ts, core/verify.ts, sandbox.ts, types.ts, core/run_turn.ts, core/agent_support.ts, docs/USER_MANUAL.md, docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, scripts/check_invariants.mjs, core/src/bin/nexus_tui/protocol.rs. NOT claimed then: security.ts, config.ts, mcp.ts, plugins.ts, doctor.ts, repl.ts, sidecar.ts, workspace_trust.ts, core/approval_policy.ts, core/command_rules.ts, core/dispatch_tool_call.ts.

- Approval mode precedence: buildConfig, cli/src/config.ts ~:440-468 (read-only > --yes (auto + fullAccess) > --approve > --mode > NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE > review). There is NO --full-access flag. Runtime changes go through NexusAgent.setApprovalMode (agent.ts ~:745-760). ApprovalPolicy.requiresDecision: cli/src/core/approval_policy.ts ~:29-88 (full access returns false first).
- MCP choke point exists: McpClientManager connections (cli/src/mcp.ts ~:606, :621, :654); the server is spawned at connect(), so a gate must sit before construction. Plugins: loadPluginFile, cli/src/plugins.ts ~:96-117; a plugin's NAME is known only after its code ran, so an allowlist must key on the file (path or SHA-256) before import().

Root-owner check precedent: cli/src/sandbox.ts ~:469. Non-blocking open: cli/src/core/checkout_trust.ts ~:32-39. writePrivateFile: cli/src/core/durable_file.ts ~:120.

## Format decision: a strict hand-written TOML SUBSET at D16's paths (/etc/nexus/policy.toml, ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml)
Why not JSON: JSON.parse silently takes the last duplicate key (`{"strict":true,"strict":false}` is false), so JSON would need a custom scanner too; TOML allows comments; D16 names .toml.
Grammar ACCEPTED: UTF-8, LF or CRLF, no BOM, no control characters except tab; blank lines; `#` comments (full-line or trailing); root `key = value` lines before any table; `[table]` headers, single level; keys and table names match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*; values: a basic string "..." on one line with only the \" and \\ escapes; true / false; a non-negative decimal integer; an array of basic strings (may span lines, trailing comma and comments allowed).
REJECTED, each with `line N`: literal or multi-line strings, any other escape; floats, signs, hex, underscores, dates; inline tables, dotted or quoted keys, [[...]], nested or mixed arrays; duplicate key, duplicate table; anything after a value except a comment; strings over 1024 characters, arrays over 500 items, files over 64 KiB.
Output {root, tables} with a line number per key; the parser is schema-agnostic; the VALIDATOR rejects unknown tables and keys. About 180-220 lines. Tests: ~25 accepted documents; ~60 rejected documents asserting line and message; render-then-parse round trip for generated documents; a mutation loop asserting only PolicyParseError is ever thrown.

## Schema: ONE normalized PolicyDocument for all tiers. Restrict-only is encoded in BOTH the types (no field can express a grant) and the merge (a lattice meet, proven by a generated table)
| Key | Type | Merge | Enforces |
|---|---|---|---|
| schema_version | int, required in managed tiers | n/a | a reader accepts only its supported set and fails closed on a higher one |
| approval.strict | bool | OR | shorthand for the next three |
| approval.disable_auto | bool | OR | mode auto from any source |
| approval.disable_yes | bool | OR | -y/--yes (including verify --yes) |
| approval.disable_full_access | bool | OR | any fullAccess source |
| approval.require_human | array of exec, write_workspace, egress | union | always ask, even under full access |
| verification.mode | approve or block ONLY | max | a floor; off and record are type errors |
| verification.protected | globs | union | extra protected paths |
| commands.forbid, commands.prompt | prefix strings such as "git push" | union | CS-9 rules; no allow key exists |
| commands.disable_allow_rules | bool | OR | drops the user's allow rules |
| paths.protected | patterns | union | |
| egress.inspector | record or block | max | floor over NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY |
| egress.allowed_domains | allowlist | intersection | |
| egress.secret_destinations | allowlist | intersection | |
| sandbox.required | bool | OR | |
| sandbox.forbid_network | bool | OR | |
| mcp.allow | allowlist: name, command:/abs/path, url:https://origin | intersection | |
| mcp.disable_workspace | bool | OR | |
| plugins.allow | allowlist: sha256:<hex>, file:/abs/path | intersection | |
| plugins.disable_workspace | bool | OR | |
| workspace.disable_env_trust | bool | OR | ignores NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE |
Allowlists: absent = unrestricted; present (even empty) = only the listed items; absent is the identity for intersection.
The project tier stays `.nexus-security.json`, mapped by an adapter into (a) a restrictive PolicyDocument part and (b) a separate ProjectRelaxations type (legacy mode off/record, verificationPaths.allow). Relaxations apply only when the workspace is trusted, integrity is MATCH, and no managed tier sets verification.mode.

## Merge and attribution
mergePolicies(system?, user?, project?) -> EffectivePolicy, frozen. Because the merge is a meet, precedence cannot change the value; it decides ATTRIBUTION only: for a scalar, the deciding tier is the highest tier whose own value equals the effective value; each list element carries the first tier that contributed it; otherwise `default`. PolicySource = {tier: "system"|"user"|"project"|"operator-rules"|"default", file?, key, line?}. One renderer describeSource -> e.g. `[policy: system /etc/nexus/policy.toml approval.strict]`; every prompt and denial appends it, including `[policy: default]` ("the effective tier is printed beside every decision").

## Modules (slice 1 = these three + tests + docs; NO existing file edited)
- cli/src/core/managed_policy.ts: pure types, validation, merge, clamp helpers, describeSource.
- cli/src/core/managed_policy_toml.ts: the parser.
- cli/src/core/managed_policy_load.ts: file-system reads with EVERY input explicit: loadManagedPolicy({systemPath, systemOwnerUid, userPath, userUid, workspace, trust, fs}). The production constant `/etc/nexus/policy.toml` lives in exactly one place, is not configurable by env, argv or setter, and that source file references neither process.env nor process.argv (a guard test asserts this).

## Fail-closed rules: both managed tiers throw ManagedPolicyError {tier, file, code, line?}
| Condition | System tier | User tier |
|---|---|---|
| File absent | tier absent | tier absent |
| /etc/nexus exists but is not root-owned, or group/world-writable, or a symlink | refuse | n/a |
| Symlink (lstat or ELOOP) | refuse | refuse |
| Not a regular file (open with O_NONBLOCK) | refuse | refuse |
| EACCES, EIO, any other error | refuse | refuse |
| Over 64 KiB | refuse | refuse |
| Owner | must be uid 0 | must be euid or 0 |
| Mode has 0o022 bits | refuse | refuse |
| fstat dev/ino differs from lstat | refuse | refuse |
| Invalid UTF-8, BOM, NUL | refuse | refuse |
| Syntax error, duplicate, unknown table or key, wrong type, bad enum | refuse | refuse |
| Empty file or missing schema_version | refuse | refuse |
| schema_version above supported | refuse | refuse |
Exit code 2 (matches existing configuration failures). Stderr, two lines:
  nexus: managed policy error (system tier): /etc/nexus/policy.toml: line 7: unknown key 'approval.disable_yess'.
  Nexus will not start without this policy. Fix the file (root-owned; ask your administrator) and run `nexus doctor`. No setting or environment variable bypasses it.
The user-tier variant ends: `Fix it, or move it aside: mv ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml ~/.config/nexus/policy.toml.bad`.
Recovery: --version, --help, `nexus doctor` and `nexus policy check` always run. The system tier has NO override of any kind. `doctor --fix` never touches policy files.

## Project integrity (principle 5)
Store ~/.config/nexus/policy_trust.json (writePrivateFile), keyed by workspace real path, value {sha256, approvedAt}. Order: bounded no-follow read -> SHA-256 -> status -> strict parse -> split into the restrictive part and relaxations. Statuses: ABSENT, NEW, MATCH, MISMATCH, REMOVED (+ ENV_TRUSTED for NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1 unless workspace.disable_env_trust). The restrictive part ALWAYS applies (as today for untrusted workspaces). Relaxations apply only on trusted and MATCH. Interactive NEW or MISMATCH with relaxations: ask, show them, record on yes. Headless: never ask; drop the relaxations, apply the restrictive part, emit a notice, record it. A project parse error stays non-fatal but becomes LOUD: built-in defaults, no relaxations, a notice, a doctor warning.

## GV-5 refusals (exit 2 at launch; runtime attempts are clamped with a notice naming the source)
--yes under disable_yes/strict; --mode auto or NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto under disable_auto; /mode auto, the "always" answer and sidecar always-approve (mode unchanged, the one call approved, notice); --sandbox none or no sandbox under sandbox.required (forced to auto + requireSandbox; explicit none refused); --sandbox-network or NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK under forbid_network; an MCP server not in mcp.allow is not started; a plugin not in plugins.allow is not imported. A managed `prompt` command rule holds under full access.

## G-3 rules
No grant is expressible; the merge is a meet; relaxations are void where a managed tier speaks. An absent tier is the identity (deleting the user or project file never goes below the system tier). Only two fixed absolute paths are read as managed; nothing under the workspace or cwd. No environment variable names a policy path; NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE, NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE, NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK, NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY are clamped AFTER the merge. lstat + O_NOFOLLOW + fstat dev/ino comparison, loaded once, frozen. Every key addition bumps schema_version (rollout order: Nexus first, then policy). Residual risks to document: an unsandboxed shell running as the user can edit the user tier and policy_trust.json for the next run (only the system tier is tamper-resistant); an admitted in-process plugin can defeat any in-process control; a bare-name mcp.allow entry is spoofable (pin with command: or url:).

## Tests (slice 1)
- managed_policy_toml.test.ts as above.
- managed_policy_merge.test.ts: GENERATED precedence table: per key, the Cartesian product of small domains across the three tiers (booleans 27 cases; list domains {absent, [], [a], [b], [a,b]} = 125 cases; verification mode also varies the project's legacy modes and trust state). Expected value and deciding tier come from an INDEPENDENT oracle per key type, not from the merge. Also idempotence, commutativity, associativity, monotonicity. "Project cannot loosen system": for every key and system value and every project document (trusted, env-trusted, legacy relaxations, malformed, absent) the effective value is at least as restrictive as the system value.
- managed_policy_load.test.ts: every row of the fail-closed table through the injected loader (fake fs / injected uids), asserting code and exact message. Guard test: the literal `/etc/nexus` appears in exactly one source file, which references neither process.env nor process.argv.
- managed_policy_integrity.test.ts: MATCH, MISMATCH, NEW, REMOVED, env trust with and without disable_env_trust; headless drops relaxations.
- Published schema (slice 1 or 4): docs/protocol/policy-v1.schema.json + POLICY_VERSIONS.json generated from PolicyDocument with cli/scripts/result_schema.mjs; a parity test.
- docs/MANAGED_POLICY.md: schema, grammar, precedence, fail-closed table, recovery path, residual risks.

## Slices
1. Pure library, NO existing source file edited (above).
2. GV-1 enforcement: config.ts, security.ts, approval_policy.ts, dispatch_tool_call.ts, command_rules.ts, workspace_trust.ts, spine_handlers.ts, completion_oracle.ts + a real-CLI test helper (interpose fs for exactly /etc/nexus and /etc/nexus/policy.toml in a child started with `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e`, as cli/test/operator_config_startup.test.ts ~:33-49 does; production keeps NO test seam).
3. GV-5: mcp.ts, plugins.ts, repl.ts, sidecar.ts, slash/session_commands.ts + strict-mode tests.
4. Visibility: doctor.ts findings policy.system|user|project|effective, new policy_cli.ts (show|check|approve), published schema.
5. Files claimed by others as they free up: index.ts, agent.ts, types.ts, sandbox.ts, core/verify.ts, protocol.ts + protocol.rs, session_export.ts, run_contract.ts, manual, changelog, the G-3 policy suite.

## Decisions taken (defaults accepted 2026-11-22)
TOML subset at D16's paths. System path is a constant, not configurable at build or run time. User tier fails closed too, with the move-aside recovery. Headless MISMATCH continues tighter (relaxations dropped), does not exit. Restrictions from an untrusted project file keep applying; relaxations never before trust and MATCH. CS-9 command_rules.json stays separate; managed tiers add forbid and prompt only. Exit code 2. Explicit flags that policy disables are refused at launch; runtime attempts are clamped with a notice. No migration needed for .nexus-security.json. Windows has no system tier (doctor says so).

## Claimed by other agents when planned (re-check before each slice; import only)
cli/src/agent.ts, index.ts, core/verify.ts, sandbox.ts, types.ts, core/run_turn.ts, core/agent_support.ts, docs/USER_MANUAL.md, docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, scripts/check_invariants.mjs, core/src/bin/nexus_tui/protocol.rs. NOT claimed then: security.ts, config.ts, mcp.ts, plugins.ts, doctor.ts, repl.ts, sidecar.ts, workspace_trust.ts, core/approval_policy.ts, core/command_rules.ts, core/dispatch_tool_call.ts.

2	
3	For the administrator of a machine or a fleet that runs Nexus.
4	
5	> **Status: enforced in part.** `nexus` reads the two managed files at startup and applies the keys listed under
6	> "What is enforced today". The MCP and plugin allowlists, `egress.secret_destinations`, the `nexus policy` commands

10	## What is enforced today
11	
12	The managed files are read once per process, before any command acts, and the result is frozen: a change to a file
13	reaches the next `nexus` process, not a running one. A project file is read per workspace and merged under the
14	managed tiers.
15	
16	| Key | Enforced | How |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `approval.strict`, `disable_auto`, `disable_yes`, `disable_full_access` | yes | An explicit `--yes`, `--mode auto` or `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` is refused at launch (exit 2). During a session a switch to `auto` (`/mode auto`, an "always" answer) is ignored with a notice, and the approval gate asks whatever the session's own settings say. In the terminal UI an "always" answer still stops later prompts in that session (planned fix, see below). |
19	| `approval.require_human` | yes | The named effects (`exec`, `write_workspace`, `egress`) ask in every mode, full access included. |
20	| `verification.mode`, `verification.protected` | yes | The mode is a floor for verification-path protection; the globs are added to the protected verification paths. A project file's relaxations are void where either key is set. |
21	| `commands.forbid` | yes | A matching `run_command` is refused in every mode. |
22	| `commands.prompt` | yes | A matching `run_command` asks in every mode, full access included; with nobody to ask it is refused. |
23	| `commands.disable_allow_rules` | yes | The `allow` rules of the operator's `command_rules.json` are not used; its `prompt` and `forbidden` rules keep working. |
24	| `paths.protected` | yes | Added to the protected path patterns of the file tools. |
25	| `egress.inspector` | yes | A floor over `NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY`. |
26	| `egress.allowed_domains` | yes, for a call that names a URL | When a managed tier sets the list, a tool call with egress effect and a `url` argument is refused unless the host is listed (an exact name, or `*.example.com` for subdomains). A call that names no URL (a web search, an MCP tool) and a shell command are not decided by this list. A project file's own `allowedDomains` keeps its existing check in the fetch tool, where a name also admits its subdomains. |
27	| `egress.secret_destinations` | not yet | Nothing reads it. |
28	| `sandbox.required` | yes, at launch | `--sandbox none` is refused; with no `--sandbox` the sandbox is switched on (`auto`), and a command is refused when no sandbox engine can run it. |
29	| `sandbox.forbid_network` | at launch only | `--sandbox-network` and a set `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK` are refused when a session is configured. The sandbox itself does not consult the policy yet. |
30	| `mcp.allow`, `mcp.disable_workspace` | not yet | Planned (GV-5). |

34	Limits of this stage:
35	
36	- `nexus verify` does not build a session configuration, so `approval.disable_yes` does not refuse `nexus verify --yes`
37	  yet, and `sandbox.*` does not reach `nexus verify --sandbox` yet (planned).
38	- The terminal UI keeps its own "always approve" state: after an "always" answer it stops asking for the rest of the
39	  session, also under `approval.disable_auto` (planned). The line-mode REPL asks every time.
40	- The sidecar started directly (not through `nexus`) reports a broken policy as a start failure with exit code 1,
41	  not 2. It still does not start.
42	- A prompt decided by the default approval mode shows no policy line; a refusal always names its source, the default
43	  included.

45	## The three tiers
46	
47	| Tier | File | Format | Who writes it |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| system | `/etc/nexus/policy.toml` | the TOML subset below | root |
50	| user | `~/.config/nexus/policy.toml` | the TOML subset below | the operator (or root) |
51	| project | `<workspace>/.nexus-security.json` | the existing JSON file | the repository |
52	
53	The system path is a constant in the code. No environment variable, command-line option or setting names another
54	path, for either managed file. Windows has no system tier.
55	
56	The system and user files are the *managed* tiers. The project file is the one Nexus already reads; its format does
57	not change and it needs no migration.
58	
59	## Restrict-only
60	
61	A policy can refuse, require a human decision, switch a convenience off, narrow an allowlist or raise a floor. It
62	cannot grant anything: there is no key that allows a command, trusts a workspace, enables a mode or lowers a
63	protection. This holds in two places.
64	
65	- **In the format.** Every key restricts when it is set. `verification.mode` accepts only `"approve"` and `"block"`;
66	  `"off"` is a type error, not a weaker setting. `[commands]` has `forbid` and `prompt` and no `allow`.
67	- **In the merge.** The tiers are combined key by key with the rule in the table below: OR for switches, union for
68	  lists of things to refuse or protect, intersection for allowlists, the maximum for floors. With these rules a tier
69	  can only make the result stricter, and a tier that is absent changes nothing. Deleting the user or the project file
70	  therefore never takes the result below the system tier.
71	
72	Precedence is **system > user > project**. Because no tier can loosen another, precedence never changes a value. It
73	decides *attribution*: which tier is named beside a decision.
74	
75	### Example 1: a switch
76	
77	System file:
78	
79	```toml
80	schema_version = 1
81	
82	[approval]
83	strict = true
84	```
85	
86	User file:
87	
88	```toml
89	schema_version = 1
90	
91	[approval]
92	strict = false
93	disable_yes = false
94	```
95	
96	Result: `strict` is true. The user file's `false` is not an override, it is the absence of a restriction. A refusal
97	of `--yes` is attributed to `[policy: system /etc/nexus/policy.toml approval.strict]`.
98	
99	### Example 2: an allowlist
100	
101	System file:
102	
103	```toml
104	schema_version = 1
105	
106	[mcp]
107	allow = ["github", "command:/usr/local/bin/mcp-files"]
108	```
109	
110	User file:
111	
112	```toml
113	schema_version = 1
114	
115	[mcp]
116	allow = ["github", "jira"]
117	```
118	
119	Result: only `github`. An allowlist entry survives only when every tier that sets the list has that same entry.
120	`jira` is not in the system list, and the system's `command:` entry is not in the user list. A user file cannot add
121	a server to the system's list; it can only take servers away.
122	
123	## Keys
124	
125	`schema_version = 1` is required as a root key in both managed files. Everything else is optional. Unknown tables and
126	unknown keys are errors.
127	
128	| Key | Type | Merge | Meaning |
129	|---|---|---|---|
130	| `schema_version` | whole number | none | The version of the format. This build supports `1`. |
131	| `approval.strict` | boolean | OR | Shorthand for the next three together. |
132	| `approval.disable_auto` | boolean | OR | Approval mode `auto` is unavailable, whatever asks for it (`--mode auto`, `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`, `/mode auto`, an "always" answer). |
133	| `approval.disable_yes` | boolean | OR | `-y` / `--yes` is unavailable. |
134	| `approval.disable_full_access` | boolean | OR | Full access is unavailable, whatever asks for it. |
135	| `approval.require_human` | array of `"exec"`, `"write_workspace"`, `"egress"` | union | These effects always need a human decision, also under full access. |
136	| `verification.mode` | `"approve"` or `"block"` | maximum (`block` > `approve`) | A floor for verification-path protection. |
137	| `verification.protected` | array of globs | union | More protected verification paths. |
138	| `commands.forbid` | array of command prefixes | union | Commands that are refused, such as `"git push"`. |
139	| `commands.prompt` | array of command prefixes | union | Commands that always ask, also under full access. |
140	| `commands.disable_allow_rules` | boolean | OR | The operator's own `allow` rules in `command_rules.json` are not used. |
141	| `paths.protected` | array of path patterns | union | More protected paths. |
142	| `egress.inspector` | `"record"` or `"block"` | maximum (`block` > `record`) | A floor for the egress inspector, above `NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY`. |
143	| `egress.allowed_domains` | allowlist of host names | intersection | The only hosts that may be reached: `"example.com"`, or `"*.example.com"` for its subdomains (not the name itself). |
144	| `egress.secret_destinations` | allowlist of origins | intersection | The only origins a credential may be sent to, such as `"https://api.example.com"`. A filter over the destinations the operator selected; it never adds one. |
145	| `sandbox.required` | boolean | OR | Commands run only in the sandbox; `--sandbox none` is refused. |
146	| `sandbox.forbid_network` | boolean | OR | Sandboxed commands get no network; `--sandbox-network` and `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK` are refused. |
147	| `mcp.allow` | allowlist | intersection | The only MCP servers that may start. An entry is a server name, `"command:/absolute/path"` or `"url:https://origin"`. |
148	| `mcp.disable_workspace` | boolean | OR | MCP servers configured by the workspace are not started. |
149	| `plugins.allow` | allowlist | intersection | The only plugin files that may be imported. An entry is `"sha256:<64 hex digits>"` or `"file:/absolute/path"`. |
150	| `plugins.disable_workspace` | boolean | OR | Plugins from the workspace are not imported. |
151	| `workspace.disable_env_trust` | boolean | OR | `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE` is ignored. |
152	
153	Notes on the types:
154	
155	- **A boolean** restricts when `true`. `false` is the same as leaving the key out.
156	- **An allowlist** that is absent means "unrestricted". One that is present, **even empty**, means "only these":
157	  `allow = []` admits nothing.
158	- **A command prefix** is command words separated by single spaces, at most 16. It matches a command, or any part of
159	  a chain (`a && b`, `a | b`), that starts with those words: `"git push"` matches `git push origin main` and not
160	  `git pushx`. `forbid` outranks `prompt`. A command hidden in `$(...)` or in a script is not seen; the sandbox is the
161	  boundary, a prefix rule is not.
162	- **Host names** are lowercase. **Origins** are written in canonical form: scheme, lowercase host, a port only when
163	  it is not the default, no path. `"https://API.example.com/"` is an error, so that the same destination is always
164	  the same string in every tier.
165	- **Paths** in `command:` and `file:` entries are absolute and normalized (no `.` or `..` segment, no doubled or
166	  trailing slash).
167	- **Duplicate items** in a list are folded into one.
168

189	prompt = ["git push", "docker run"]
190	disable_allow_rules = false

192	[paths]

194	
195	[egress]

198	  "example.com",

200	]
201	secret_destinations = ["https://gateway.example.com"]
202	
203	[sandbox]
204	required = true
205	forbid_network = false
206	
207	[mcp]
208	allow = [
209	  "command:/usr/local/bin/mcp-files",
210	  "url:https://mcp.example.com",
211	]
212	disable_workspace = true
213	
214	[plugins]
215	allow = ["sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"]

220	```
221	
222	A JSON Schema of the same data (each table an object) is published as `docs/protocol/policy-v1.schema.json` for an
223	editor or a linter. It describes shape only and is looser than Nexus's own validator: it does not reject unknown
224	keys, and it does not check the form of list items.
225	
226	## The file format
227	
228	A managed file is a small, strict subset of TOML.
229	
230	Accepted:
231	
232	- UTF-8 text with LF or CRLF line ends; blank lines; `#` comments on their own line or after a value or a table
233	  header;
234	- `key = value` lines, at the top of the file (root keys) or under a table header;
235	- `[table]` headers, one level deep;
236	- keys and table names made of lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter;
237	- values: a basic string `"..."` on one line, with only the escapes `\"` and `\\`; `true` or `false`; a
238	  non-negative decimal whole number; an array of basic strings, which may span lines and may have a trailing comma
239	  and comments.
240	
241	Rejected, each with the line number:
242	
243	- literal strings (`'...'`), multi-line strings, any escape other than `\"` and `\\`;
244	- floats, signed numbers, hexadecimal, octal and binary numbers, digit separators (`1_000`), leading zeros, dates
245	  and times;
246	- inline tables (`{ ... }`), dotted keys (`a.b = 1`), quoted keys, dotted table names, arrays of tables (`[[x]]`);
247	- arrays of anything but strings, nested arrays;
248	- a key set twice in a table, a table defined twice;
249	- anything after a value or a table header other than a comment;
250	- a byte-order mark, a NUL or any control character other than tab, a carriage return that is not part of CRLF;
251	- a string longer than 1024 characters, an array of more than 500 items, a file larger than 64 KiB.
252	
253	**Why the subset is strict.** A policy file restricts. If the reader skipped a construct it did not understand, or
254	took the last of two definitions of a key, a file could say one thing to the person reviewing it and another to
255	Nexus, and the difference would always be a missing restriction. So there is one way to write each thing, nothing is
256	skipped, and a file that is not understood completely is refused completely. A general TOML library would accept much
257	more than a policy needs; JSON was not used because the standard JSON reader silently keeps the last duplicate key.
258	
259	What a rejected file looks like, and what is reported:
260	
261	```text
262	schema_version = 1
263	[approval]
264	strict = yes            <- line 3: unsupported value 'yes': expected a "string", true, false, a whole number or an array of strings
265	approval.strict = true  <- dotted keys are not supported; put the key under a [table] header
266	mode = 'block'          <- literal strings ('...') are not supported; use a basic string "..."
267	```
268	
269	## Fail closed
270	
271	A managed file that exists must be read, checked, parsed and validated completely. If any step fails the loader
272	throws; it never returns a default or a partly read policy in place of a file it could not use. Only a file that does
273	not exist counts as "no policy in this tier".
274	
275	| Condition | System tier | User tier |
276	|---|---|---|
277	| The file does not exist | tier absent | tier absent |
278	| `/etc/nexus` exists and is not owned by root, or is writable by group or others, or is a symbolic link, or is not a directory, or cannot be inspected | refuse (even when it holds no policy file) | not checked |
279	| The file is a symbolic link | refuse | refuse |
280	| The path is not a regular file (a directory, a FIFO, a device) | refuse | refuse |
281	| The file cannot be inspected, opened or read (`EACCES`, `EIO`, any other error) | refuse | refuse |
282	| The file is larger than 64 KiB | refuse | refuse |
283	| Owner | must be root (uid 0) | must be the user running Nexus, or root |
284	| The file is writable by group or others | refuse | refuse |
285	| The file changed between the first check and the open (different device or inode, or it vanished) | refuse | refuse |
286	| Invalid UTF-8, a byte-order mark, a NUL byte | refuse | refuse |
287	| A syntax error, a duplicate key or table, an unknown table or key, a wrong type, a value outside an enumeration, a malformed list item | refuse | refuse |
288	| An empty file (also one with comments only), or no `schema_version` | refuse | refuse |
289	| A `schema_version` this build does not support | refuse | refuse |
290	
291	The file is opened without following a symbolic link and without blocking, and the checks of owner, mode and size
292	are made on the opened file. On a platform without POSIX owners the owner and mode checks do not apply.
293	
294	The system tier is checked first; when both managed files are broken, the system error is the one reported.
295	
296	### The error
297	
298	The loader's error carries the tier, the file, a code and (for a content error) the line, and this two-line message
299	for stderr. The process exit code reserved for it is 2, the same as other configuration failures.
300	
301	System tier:
302	
303	```text
304	nexus: managed policy error (system tier): /etc/nexus/policy.toml: line 7: unknown key 'approval.disable_yess'.
305	Nexus will not start without this policy. Fix the file (root-owned; ask your administrator) and run `nexus doctor`. No setting or environment variable bypasses it.
306	```
307	
308	User tier (the path is the real path of the file, quoted when it needs quoting):
309	
310	```text
311	nexus: managed policy error (user tier): /home/ada/.config/nexus/policy.toml: line 4: duplicate key 'approval.strict' (first set on line 3); a key may be set once.
312	Nexus will not start without this policy. Fix it, or move it aside: mv /home/ada/.config/nexus/policy.toml /home/ada/.config/nexus/policy.toml.bad
313	```
314	
315	The first line is always `nexus: managed policy error (<tier> tier): <file>: [line N: ]<what is wrong>.` The texts
316	for the conditions that are not about a line:
317	
318	| Code | What is wrong |
319	|---|---|
320	| `directory_unsafe` | `the directory /etc/nexus is owned by uid 1000; it must be owned by root (uid 0)`; `... is writable by group or others (mode 775)`; `... is a symbolic link`; `/etc/nexus is not a directory`; `cannot inspect the directory /etc/nexus (EACCES)` |
321	| `symlink` | `the file is a symbolic link; it must be a regular file` |
322	| `not_regular` | `the path is not a regular file` |
323	| `unreadable` | `cannot inspect the file (EACCES)`; `cannot open the file (EACCES)`; `cannot read the file (EIO)` |
324	| `changed` | `the file was replaced while it was being read`; `the file was removed while it was being read` |
325	| `owner` | `the file is owned by uid 1000; it must be owned by root (uid 0)`; for the user tier `... it must be owned by you (uid 1000) or root` |
326	| `mode` | `the file is writable by group or others (mode 664); run chmod go-w on it` |
327	| `too_large` | `the file is larger than 64 KiB` |
328	| `invalid_utf8`, `bom`, `nul` | `the file is not valid UTF-8`; `the file starts with a byte-order mark; save it as UTF-8 without a BOM`; `the file contains a NUL byte` |
329	| `empty` | ``the file is empty; a policy file needs at least the line `schema_version = 1` `` |
330	| `schema_version_missing` | ``schema_version is missing; add `schema_version = 1` as the first line`` |
331	
332	Content errors name the line: `syntax`, `unsupported`, `duplicate_key`, `duplicate_table`, `string_too_long`,
333	`array_too_long`, `control_character`, `invalid_unicode` from the parser; `unknown_table`, `unknown_key`,
334	`wrong_type`, `bad_value`, `schema_version_unsupported` from the validator. Examples:
335	
336	```text
337	line 3: unknown table '[aproval]'
338	line 3: unknown key 'commands.allow'
339	line 3: key 'sandbox.required' must be true or false
340	line 3: key 'verification.mode' must be "approve" or "block" (found "off"); a policy can only raise this, never lower it
341	line 5: key 'mcp.allow', item 2 ("cmd:/x") must be a server name (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), "command:/absolute/path" or "url:https://origin"
342	line 2: schema_version 2 is not supported by this Nexus (supported: 1); upgrade Nexus before rolling out this policy
343	```
344	
345	## Recovery
346	
347	- **What still runs when a tier is broken:** `nexus --version`, `nexus --help` and `nexus doctor` (and its alias
348	  `nexus check`). Everything else exits with code 2 and the message above. `nexus doctor` has no policy findings of
349	  its own yet: it shows the error in its configuration finding. A `nexus policy check` command is planned.
350	- **The system tier has no bypass.** No flag, environment variable, user setting or project file makes Nexus run
351	  past a system file it cannot use. The only fix is to repair or remove the file as root. This is the lockout risk
352	  of a managed policy: a typing mistake in a file pushed to a fleet stops Nexus on every machine that receives it.
353	  Until `nexus policy check` exists there is no supported command to test a file before rolling it out.
354	- **The user tier** fails closed too, and the user can recover alone: fix the file, or move it aside with the `mv`
355	  command the message prints. With the file gone the user tier is absent and the system tier still applies in full.
356	- **Replace a policy file atomically** (write a new file beside it, then rename). A file caught half written is
357	  either refused, or, if the written part happens to be a complete valid policy, read as that shorter policy.
358	- **`schema_version` and rollout order.** Every added or changed key bumps the version, and a reader refuses a
359	  version it does not know. Upgrade Nexus first, then roll out a policy that uses the new version.
360	- `nexus doctor --fix` is not to modify a policy file (planned).
361	
362	## The project file and its integrity
363	
364	`.nexus-security.json` is written by the repository, so it is treated as two parts.
365	
366	- **Restrictions** (`protectedPaths`, `allowedDomains`, `verificationPaths.mode` of `approve` or `block`,
367	  `verificationPaths.extra`) join the merge like any tier. They apply in every workspace, trusted or not, approved or
368	  not. `blockedCommands` are substring patterns of the destructive-command tripwire, not command prefixes; they are
369	  passed through unchanged and are not turned into `commands.forbid` rules.
370	- **Relaxations** are the two settings that weaken verification protection: `verificationPaths.mode` of `off` or
371	  `record`, and `verificationPaths.allow`. They are kept apart from the merge and apply only when **all** of these
372	  hold:
373	  1. the workspace is trusted by the operator **and** the file is byte for byte the one the operator approved
374	     (status `MATCH`), or `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1` is set and no managed tier sets `workspace.disable_env_trust`
375	     (status `ENV_TRUSTED`);
376	  2. no managed tier sets any key under `[verification]`. Where a managed tier speaks about verification, the
377	     project's relaxations are void, in every trust state.
378	
379	A project file cannot set any other key: there is no way to write `approval`, `sandbox`, `mcp`, `plugins`,
380	`workspace` or an egress-inspector setting from a repository.
381	
382	The file's bytes are hashed (SHA-256) before anything parses them. The hash is compared with the one recorded for the
383	workspace in `~/.config/nexus/policy_trust.json` (mode 0600, keyed by the workspace's real path):
384	
385	| Status | Meaning | Relaxations |
386	|---|---|---|
387	| `ABSENT` | no project file, none approved before | none to apply |
388	| `NEW` | a project file that was never approved | not applied |
389	| `MATCH` | the file is the approved one | applied when the workspace is also trusted |
390	| `MISMATCH` | the file differs from the approved one | not applied |
391	| `REMOVED` | a file was approved and there is none now | none to apply; reported |
392	| `ENV_TRUSTED` | `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1`, not disabled by policy | applied |
393	| `UNREADABLE` | the file is a symbolic link, not a regular file, larger than 64 KiB, or cannot be read | not applied; reported |
394	
395	- **How a file is approved.** Trusting the workspace is the approval: `nexus trust <workspace>` (and the trust
396	  question an interactive start asks) records the hash of the file as it is at that moment. A file that changes
397	  afterwards is `MISMATCH` until `nexus trust <workspace>` is run again. A workspace that was trusted before this
398	  release has no recorded hash, so its file is `NEW`: its relaxations stay off until the workspace is trusted again.
399	  Nexus does not yet show the relaxations when it records an approval, and does not yet ask in the middle of a
400	  session (planned); read the file before you trust the workspace.
401	- **A headless run** is never asked and never stopped by the project file. The relaxations are dropped, the
402	  restrictions apply, and a notice says which status caused it. The run continues tighter, not looser.
403	- **A project file that cannot be parsed** is not fatal, because it cannot loosen a managed tier, but it is loud:
404	  none of the file is used (the managed tiers and the built-in defaults still apply), and a notice says so.
405	- **Notices** go to standard error, each once per process.
406	- A broken `policy_trust.json` approves nothing, and is reported.
407	
408	## Decisions carry their source
409	
410	Every decision the helpers return names the tier it comes from, in one form:
411	
412	```text
413	[policy: system /etc/nexus/policy.toml approval.strict]
414	[policy: user /home/ada/.config/nexus/policy.toml mcp.allow]
415	[policy: project /work/app/.nexus-security.json verificationPaths.mode]
416	[policy: default]
417	```
418	
419	For a switch or a floor, the tier named is the highest tier whose own value is the effective value. For a list, each
420	item carries the highest tier that lists it. For a refusal by an allowlist, the tier named is the highest tier whose
421	own list excludes the thing refused.
422	
423	The refusal and notice texts of the admin controls (GV-5), as the helpers produce them:
424	
425	```text
426	--yes is refused: managed policy disables it. [policy: ...]
427	--yes is refused: it selects approval mode 'auto', which managed policy disables. [policy: ...]
428	--yes is refused: it grants full access, which managed policy disables. [policy: ...]
429	--mode auto is refused: managed policy disables approval mode 'auto'. [policy: ...]
430	NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto is refused: managed policy disables approval mode 'auto'. [policy: ...]
431	<what asked> is refused: managed policy disables full access. [policy: ...]
432	/mode auto is ignored: managed policy disables approval mode 'auto'; the mode stays 'review'. [policy: ...]
433	'always' is not remembered: managed policy disables approval mode 'auto'; this one call is approved. [policy: ...]
434	approval required: managed policy requires a human decision for exec, also under full access. [policy: ...]
435	--sandbox none is refused: managed policy requires the sandbox. [policy: ...]
436	the sandbox is on (auto): managed policy requires it. [policy: ...]
437	--sandbox-network is refused: managed policy forbids network access in the sandbox. [policy: ...]
438	MCP server 'shell' is not started: it is not in the managed allowlist (mcp.allow). [policy: ...]
439	MCP server 'shell' is not started: managed policy disables MCP servers configured by the workspace. [policy: ...]
440	plugin '/ws/plugins/x.mjs' is not imported: it is not in the managed allowlist (plugins.allow). [policy: ...]
441	plugin '/ws/plugins/x.mjs' is not imported: managed policy disables plugins from the workspace. [policy: ...]
442	command refused: managed policy forbids 'git push'. [policy: ...]
443	approval required: managed policy asks before 'npm publish', also under full access. [policy: ...]
444	the egress inspector runs in 'block' mode, not 'off': managed policy sets the floor. [policy: ...]
445	NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE is ignored: managed policy disables it. [policy: ...]
446	```
447	
448	A flag that policy disables is refused at launch (exit code 2); an attempt during a session is clamped with a notice
449	and the session continues. The texts for MCP servers and plugins are not produced yet (see "What is enforced
450	today"). A runtime switch to `auto` is reported as `A request for approval mode 'auto' is ignored: ...`.
451	
452	## What a policy does not protect against
453	
454	- **Only the system tier is tamper-resistant.** The user file and `policy_trust.json` belong to the user. A shell
455	  that runs as the user outside the sandbox can edit or delete them, and the next run sees the change. Put what must
456	  hold in the system file, and require the sandbox there.
457	- **An admitted plugin runs inside the Nexus process** and can defeat any control that process applies. An entry in
458	  `plugins.allow` is a decision to trust that code completely; prefer `sha256:` entries, which pin the content.
459	- **A bare name in `mcp.allow` is spoofable.** Whoever can write an MCP configuration can give any program the name
460	  `github`. Pin a server with `command:/absolute/path` or `url:https://origin`.
461	- **A `file:` or `command:` entry trusts whatever is at that path**; protect the path with file permissions.
462	- **An approved project file can still relax the built-in default.** When no managed tier sets anything under
463	  `[verification]`, a trusted workspace whose file the operator approved may set `verificationPaths.mode` to `off`
464	  or `record`, as it can today. To rule that out, set `verification.mode` in a managed file.
465	- **Allowlists are intersected as text.** `"*.example.com"` in one tier and `"api.example.com"` in another have no
466	  entry in common, so the result admits nothing. That errs on the strict side, but it can surprise.
467	- **Command prefixes are not a sandbox** (see the note on prefixes above).
468	- **A valid file is taken at its word.** The checks stop a file that cannot be understood; they cannot tell a policy
469	  that was meant to be longer from one that is complete.
470	- **The published JSON Schema is looser than the validator** (see above); passing it does not mean Nexus accepts the
471	  file.
472
